literal: Those who have nothing, everyone will despise; the wealthy, everyone will do honor.
translation: Everyone despises those who have nothing, while everyone shows honor and respect to the wealthy.
modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்களை எல்லாரும் இகழ்ந்து பேசுவார்கள்; செல்வம் உடையவர்களை எல்லாரும் மதித்துச் சிறப்பு செய்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights a stark social reality regarding how wealth dictates human relationships and societal respect. The author observes that those who lack material wealth (illārai) are universally looked down upon or despised (eḷḷuvar) by everyone. Conversely, those who possess wealth (celvarai) are universally honored and treated with high regard (ciṟappu ceyvar). By contrasting the verbs 'eḷḷuvar' (despise) and 'ceyvar ciṟappu' (will do honor), the verse emphasizes that wealth is a primary driver of social standing and influence.
